/-!
# Exact upper–lower–upper collision fibres over commutative rings

Every parameter collision is an annihilator translation (a+t,c-t), with b*t=0.
The sum of the two outer parameters is conserved. An explicit fibre equivalence
therefore gives exact multiplicity over composite residue rings, retaining nonunits
and the zero ring without a field or cancellation assumption.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.FiniteUnipotentFibres
open FiniteRingSl2
noncomputable section
variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The actual three elementary factors in the determinant-one group. -/
def triple (a b c : R) : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) R := upper a*lower b*upper c

/-- The first diagonal entry of the actual three-factor word. -/
theorem triple_entry00 (a b c : R) : triple a b c 0 0=1+a*b := by
  simp [triple,upper,lower,Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul,Matrix.mul_apply,Fin.sum_univ_two]

/-- The complete upper-right entry, retaining its mixed product. -/
theorem triple_entry01 (a b c : R) : triple a b c 0 1=a+c+a*b*c := by
  simp [triple,upper,lower,Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul,Matrix.mul_apply,Fin.sum_univ_two]
  ring

/-- The lower entry recovers the middle parameter exactly. -/
theorem triple_entry10 (a b c : R) : triple a b c 1 0=b := by
  simp [triple,upper,lower,Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul,Matrix.mul_apply,Fin.sum_univ_two]

/-- The second diagonal entry of the actual three-factor word. -/
theorem triple_entry11 (a b c : R) : triple a b c 1 1=1+b*c := by
  simp [triple,upper,lower,Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.coe_mul,Matrix.mul_apply,Fin.sum_univ_two]
  ring

/-- Complete collision classification at any fixed middle parameter, including nonunits. -/
theorem triple_collision (a b c a' c' : R) :
    triple a' b c'=triple a b c ↔ b*(a'-a)=0 ∧ a'+c'=a+c := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h00 := congrArg (fun M : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) R => M 0 0) h
    have h01 := congrArg (fun M : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) R => M 0 1) h
    have h11 := congrArg (fun M : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) R => M 1 1) h
    rw [triple_entry00,triple_entry00] at h00
    rw [triple_entry01,triple_entry01] at h01
    rw [triple_entry11,triple_entry11] at h11
    constructor
    · linear_combination h00
    · linear_combination h01-c'*h00-a*h11
  · rintro ⟨hb,hs⟩
    apply Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.ext
    intro i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
    · change triple a' b c' 0 0=triple a b c 0 0
      rw [triple_entry00,triple_entry00]
      linear_combination hb
    · change triple a' b c' 0 1=triple a b c 0 1
      rw [triple_entry01,triple_entry01]
      linear_combination (1+a*b)*hs+(c'-a)*hb
    · change triple a' b c' 1 0=triple a b c 1 0
      rw [triple_entry10,triple_entry10]
    · change triple a' b c' 1 1=triple a b c 1 1
      rw [triple_entry11,triple_entry11]
      linear_combination b*hs-hb

/-- Every annihilator translation preserves the actual three-factor word. -/
theorem triple_translate (a b c t : R) (ht : b*t=0) :
    triple (a+t) b (c-t)=triple a b c := by
  apply (triple_collision a b c (a+t) (c-t)).mpr
  constructor
  · simpa using ht
  · ring

/-- The full parameter fibre is explicitly equivalent to the middle-parameter annihilator. -/
def fibreEquiv (a b c : R) :
    {t : R // b*t=0} ≃ {u : R×R // triple u.1 b u.2=triple a b c} where
  toFun t := ⟨(a+t.1,c-t.1),triple_translate a b c t.1 t.2⟩
  invFun u := ⟨u.1.1-a,((triple_collision a b c u.1.1 u.1.2).mp u.2).1⟩
  left_inv t := by apply Subtype.ext; simp
  right_inv u := by
    apply Subtype.ext
    apply Prod.ext
    · simp
    · have hs := ((triple_collision a b c u.1.1 u.1.2).mp u.2).2
      dsimp
      linear_combination -hs

/-- The exact fibre multiplicity is the cardinality of the annihilator. -/
theorem fibre_card (a b c : R) :
    Nat.card {u : R×R // triple u.1 b u.2=triple a b c}=Nat.card {t : R // b*t=0} :=
  (Nat.card_congr (fibreEquiv a b c)).symm


/-- Every full collision fixes the middle parameter and conserves the outer sum. -/
theorem triple_collision_full (a b c a' b' c' : R) :
    triple a' b' c'=triple a b c ↔ b'=b ∧ b*(a'-a)=0 ∧ a'+c'=a+c := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hb := congrArg (fun M : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) R => M 1 0) h
    rw [triple_entry10,triple_entry10] at hb
    subst b'
    exact ⟨rfl,(triple_collision a b c a' c').mp h⟩
  · rintro ⟨hb,h⟩
    rw [hb]
    exact (triple_collision a b c a' c').mpr h

end

/-! # A uniform perturbation bound for the cubic Hankel determinant -/
namespace HTGeometry
noncomputable section

private theorem triple_product_error {a b c A B C M δ : ℝ}
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hb : |b| ≤ M) (hc : |c| ≤ M) (hA : |A| ≤ M) (hB : |B| ≤ M)
    (haA : |a-A| ≤ δ) (hbB : |b-B| ≤ δ) (hcC : |c-C| ≤ δ) :
    |a*b*c-A*B*C| ≤ 3*M^2*δ := by
  have h1 : |(a-A)*b*c| ≤ δ*M*M := by
    simp only [abs_mul]
    exact mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul haA hb (abs_nonneg _) hδ) hc (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity)
  have h2 : |A*(b-B)*c| ≤ M*δ*M := by
    simp only [abs_mul]
    exact mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul hA hbB (abs_nonneg _) hM) hc (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity)
  have h3 : |A*B*(c-C)| ≤ M*M*δ := by
    simp only [abs_mul]
    exact mul_le_mul (mul_le_mul hA hB (abs_nonneg _) hM) hcC (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity)
  rw [show a*b*c-A*B*C = (a-A)*b*c+A*(b-B)*c+A*B*(c-C) by ring]
  have ht := abs_add_le ((a-A)*b*c+A*(b-B)*c) (A*B*(c-C))
  have ht' := abs_add_le ((a-A)*b*c) (A*(b-B)*c)
  nlinarith only [h1, h2, h3, ht, ht']

/-- Entrywise errors at most delta on two bounded tuples change the determinant by at most
`18 M² delta`; the bound accounts for all six signed cubic monomials. -/
theorem signedEvenHankelThreeDet_error_le
    {a b c d e A B C D E M δ : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hp : |a| ≤ M ∧ |b| ≤ M ∧ |c| ≤ M ∧ |d| ≤ M ∧ |e| ≤ M)
    (hq : |A| ≤ M ∧ |B| ≤ M ∧ |C| ≤ M ∧ |D| ≤ M ∧ |E| ≤ M)
    (he : |a-A| ≤ δ ∧ |b-B| ≤ δ ∧ |c-C| ≤ δ ∧ |d-D| ≤ δ ∧ |e-E| ≤ δ) :
    |HilbertMetric.signedEvenHankelThreeDet a b c d e -
      HilbertMetric.signedEvenHankelThreeDet A B C D E| ≤ 18*M^2*δ := by
  rcases hp with ⟨ha, hb, hc, hd, he'⟩
  rcases hq with ⟨hA, hB, hC, hD, hE⟩
  rcases he with ⟨haA, hbB, hcC, hdD, heE⟩
  have h1 := triple_product_error hM hδ hc he' hA hC haA hcC heE
  have h2 := triple_product_error hM hδ hd hd hA hD haA hdD hdD
  have h3 := triple_product_error hM hδ hb he' hB hB hbB hbB heE
  have h4 := triple_product_error hM hδ hc hd hB hC hbB hcC hdD
  have h5 := triple_product_error hM hδ hc hc hC hC hcC hcC hcC
  have hb1 := abs_le.mp h1
  have hb2 := abs_le.mp h2
  have hb3 := abs_le.mp h3
  have hb4 := abs_le.mp h4
  have hb5 := abs_le.mp h5
  apply abs_le.mpr
  unfold HilbertMetric.signedEvenHankelThreeDet
  constructor <;> nlinarith only [hb1.1, hb1.2, hb2.1, hb2.2, hb3.1, hb3.2,
    hb4.1, hb4.2, hb5.1, hb5.2]

end
end HTGeometry

/-!
# The cocycle identity for the torsor comparison matrix

Inside the triple tensor product the three copies of an invertible fundamental solution matrix are
compared pairwise by the comparison matrix, and the three comparisons satisfy

```
    Z₁₃ = Z₁₂ · Z₂₃ ,
```

because `Y₁ Z₁₂ = Y₂`, `Y₂ Z₂₃ = Y₃` and `Y₁ Z₁₃ = Y₃`, and `Y₁` is invertible.  This is the group
law of the difference Galois group: it is what makes the functor of points of the comparison matrix
a monoid over *every* base algebra, not only over the field of constants.

* `tensor12`, `tensor23`, `tensor13` — the three inclusions of the tensor square;
* `torsor_cocycle` — **the identity.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

open scoped TensorProduct

variable (K R : Type*) [Field K] [CommRing R] [Algebra K R]

/-- The inclusion of the tensor square into the first two factors of the triple tensor product. -/
def tensor12 : (R ⊗[K] R) →ₐ[K] ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft

/-- The inclusion of the tensor square into the last two factors of the triple tensor product. -/
def tensor23 : (R ⊗[K] R) →ₐ[K] ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : R →ₐ[K] R ⊗[K] R)
    (AlgHom.id K R)

/-- The inclusion of the tensor square into the outer two factors of the triple tensor product. -/
def tensor13 : (R ⊗[K] R) →ₐ[K] ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : R →ₐ[K] R ⊗[K] R)
    (AlgHom.id K R)

variable {K R}

@[simp] theorem tensor12_tmul (a b : R) :
    tensor12 K R (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) = (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R) := rfl

@[simp] theorem tensor23_tmul (a b : R) :
    tensor23 K R (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) = ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[K] a) ⊗ₜ[K] b := rfl

@[simp] theorem tensor13_tmul (a b : R) :
    tensor13 K R (a ⊗ₜ[K] b) = (a ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R)) ⊗ₜ[K] b := rfl

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The three copies of the fundamental matrix inside the triple tensor product. -/
def tripleFundamental₁ (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Y.map fun a => (a ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R)) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R)

def tripleFundamental₂ (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Y.map fun a => ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[K] a) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R)

def tripleFundamental₃ (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
  Y.map fun a => ((1 : R) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : R)) ⊗ₜ[K] a

theorem map_leftFundamental_tensor12 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (leftFundamental K Y).map (tensor12 K R) = tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y := rfl

theorem map_rightFundamental_tensor12 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (rightFundamental K Y).map (tensor12 K R) = tripleFundamental₂ (K := K) Y := rfl

theorem map_leftFundamental_tensor23 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (leftFundamental K Y).map (tensor23 K R) = tripleFundamental₂ (K := K) Y := rfl

theorem map_rightFundamental_tensor23 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (rightFundamental K Y).map (tensor23 K R) = tripleFundamental₃ (K := K) Y := rfl

theorem map_leftFundamental_tensor13 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (leftFundamental K Y).map (tensor13 K R) = tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y := rfl

theorem map_rightFundamental_tensor13 (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    (rightFundamental K Y).map (tensor13 K R) = tripleFundamental₃ (K := K) Y := rfl

/-- **The cocycle identity.**  Inside the triple tensor product the comparison matrix satisfies the
group law `Z₁₃ = Z₁₂ · Z₂₃`. -/
theorem torsor_cocycle (Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hY : IsUnit Y.det)
    (Z : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (R ⊗[K] R))
    (hZ : leftFundamental K Y * Z = rightFundamental K Y) :
    Z.map (tensor13 K R) = Z.map (tensor12 K R) * Z.map (tensor23 K R) := by
  have h12 : tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y * Z.map (tensor12 K R)
      = tripleFundamental₂ (K := K) Y := by
    rw [← map_leftFundamental_tensor12, ← map_rightFundamental_tensor12, ← Matrix.map_mul, hZ]
  have h23 : tripleFundamental₂ (K := K) Y * Z.map (tensor23 K R)
      = tripleFundamental₃ (K := K) Y := by
    rw [← map_leftFundamental_tensor23, ← map_rightFundamental_tensor23, ← Matrix.map_mul, hZ]
  have h13 : tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y * Z.map (tensor13 K R)
      = tripleFundamental₃ (K := K) Y := by
    rw [← map_leftFundamental_tensor13, ← map_rightFundamental_tensor13, ← Matrix.map_mul, hZ]
  set φ : R →ₐ[K] ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R) :=
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : (R ⊗[K] R) →ₐ[K] ((R ⊗[K] R) ⊗[K] R)).comp
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : R →ₐ[K] R ⊗[K] R) with hφ
  have hY1 : IsUnit (tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y).det := by
    have hmap : (tripleFundamental₁ (K := K) Y).det = φ Y.det :=

@[simp]
theorem cross_anticomm (v w : Fin 3 → R) : -(v ⨯₃ w) = w ⨯₃ v := by
  simp [cross_apply, mul_comm]

alias neg_cross := cross_anticomm

@[simp]
theorem cross_anticomm' (v w : Fin 3 → R) : v ⨯₃ w + w ⨯₃ v = 0 := by
  rw [add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg, cross_anticomm]

@[simp]
theorem cross_self (v : Fin 3 → R) : v ⨯₃ v = 0 := by
  simp [cross_apply, mul_comm]

/-- The cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to the first vector. -/
@[simp]
theorem dot_self_cross (v w : Fin 3 → R) : v ⬝ᵥ v ⨯₃ w = 0 := by
  rw [cross_apply, vec3_dotProduct]
  dsimp only [Matrix.cons_val]
  ring

/-- The cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to the second vector. -/
@[simp]
theorem dot_cross_self (v w : Fin 3 → R) : w ⬝ᵥ v ⨯₃ w = 0 := by
  rw [← cross_anticomm, dotProduct_neg, dot_self_cross, neg_zero]

/-- Cyclic permutations preserve the triple product. See also `triple_product_eq_det`. -/
theorem triple_product_permutation (u v w : Fin 3 → R) : u ⬝ᵥ v ⨯₃ w = v ⬝ᵥ w ⨯₃ u := by
  simp_rw [cross_apply, vec3_dotProduct]
  dsimp only [Matrix.cons_val]
  ring

/-- The triple product of `u`, `v`, and `w` is equal to the determinant of the matrix
with those vectors as its rows. -/
theorem triple_product_eq_det (u v w : Fin 3 → R) : u ⬝ᵥ v ⨯₃ w = Matrix.det ![u, v, w] := by
  rw [vec3_dotProduct, cross_apply, det_fin_three]
  dsimp only [Matrix.cons_val]
  ring

/-- The scalar quadruple product identity, related to the Binet-Cauchy identity. -/
theorem cross_dot_cross (u v w x : Fin 3 → R) :
    u ⨯₃ v ⬝ᵥ w ⨯₃ x = u ⬝ᵥ w * v ⬝ᵥ x - u ⬝ᵥ x * v ⬝ᵥ w := by
  simp_rw [cross_apply, vec3_dotProduct]
  dsimp only [Matrix.cons_val]
  ring

end ProductsProperties

section LeibnizProperties

/-- The cross product satisfies the Leibniz lie property. -/
theorem leibniz_cross (u v w : Fin 3 → R) : u ⨯₃ (v ⨯₃ w) = u ⨯₃ v ⨯₃ w + v ⨯₃ (u ⨯₃ w) := by
  simp_rw [cross_apply, vec3_add]
  apply vec3_eq <;> dsimp <;> ring

/-- The three-dimensional vectors together with the operations + and ⨯₃ form a Lie ring.
Note we do not make this an instance as a conflicting one already exists
via `LieRing.ofAssociativeRing`. -/
@[instance_reducible]
def Cross.lieRing : LieRing (Fin 3 → R) :=
  { Pi.addCommGroup with
    bracket := fun u v => u ⨯₃ v
    add_lie := LinearMap.map_add₂ _
    lie_add := fun _ => map_add _
    lie_self := cross_self
    leibniz_lie := leibniz_cross }

attribute [local instance] Cross.lieRing

theorem cross_cross (u v w : Fin 3 → R) : u ⨯₃ v ⨯₃ w = u ⨯₃ (v ⨯₃ w) - v ⨯₃ (u ⨯₃ w) :=
  lie_lie u v w

/-- **Jacobi identity**: For a cross product of three vectors,
their sum over the three even permutations is equal to the zero vector. -/
theorem jacobi_cross (u v w : Fin 3 → R) : u ⨯₃ (v ⨯₃ w) + v ⨯₃ (w ⨯₃ u) + w ⨯₃ (u ⨯₃ v) = 0 :=
  lie_jacobi u v w

end LeibnizProperties

/-- The scalar triple product expansion of the vector triple product. -/
theorem cross_cross_eq_smul_sub_smul (u v w : Fin 3 → R) :
    u ⨯₃ v ⨯₃ w = (u ⬝ᵥ w) • v - (v ⬝ᵥ w) • u := by
  simp_rw [cross_apply, vec3_dotProduct]
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;>
  · simp only [Fin.isValue, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val,
      Pi.sub_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    ring

  simp_rw [cross_apply, vec3_dotProduct]
  ext i
